content:
maria: Quick heads-up — traces are getting fragmented for requests routed to the EU GPU pool (eu-west-1). Root span shows at the gateway, but runtime/kv and GPU spans are missing downstream, especially for long seq_len workloads.
ashok: Is this new after any infra change?
mar ia: typo — maria: yes, we added an nginx layer in front of Envoy a week ago for cert management.
leo: nginx is a common culprit — it can truncate long headers (baggage) or drop `traceparent` if configured to sanitize. Are we using W3C (traceparent/tracestate) or B3?
jordan: We standardize on W3C across SDKs (java/python/go).
park: I saw some logs where the runtime receives requests without `traceparent` header. The SDKs include it, so something in the path is stripping.
sre-ops: Any correlation with GPU eviction / long tails? Could also be timeouts in the runtime that cut a running span before child spans flush.
maria: It's mostly long-running inferences (>800ms) and multi-request-chat flows (streaming). Short single-turn calls show full traces.
leo: Two issues to investigate in parallel: 1) propagation through LB/proxies (headers) and 2) batching/flush behavior in the runtime SDKs when holding onto spans during streaming.
ashok: For (1) check Envoy/nginx config to forward these headers explicitly. Example envoy route config we should ensure exists:
```yaml
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.router
  - name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_add
    typed_config:
      '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_add.v3.HeaderToAdd
      request_headers_to_add:
        - header:
            key: traceparent
            value: "%REQ(traceparent)%"
        - header:
            key: tracestate
            value: "%REQ(tracestate)%"
        - header:
            key: baggage
            value: "%REQ(baggage)%"
```
park: For nginx fronting Envoy we also need `large_client_header_buffers` and `proxy_set_header` lines:
```nginx
http {
  large_client_header_buffers 4 32k;
  server {
    location / {
      proxy_pass http://envoy;
      proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;
      proxy_set_header Tracestate $http_tracestate;
      proxy_set_header Baggage $http_baggage;
    }
  }
}
```
jordan: Good. For (2) the runtime uses otel-java auto-instrumentation + exporter batching. Streaming flush is sometimes delayed by the batcher so child spans never make it if process is short-lived. We should tweak exporter batch/flush settings for the inference process.
leo: Also consider server-side (collector) tail-based sampling: let SDKs always send trace events, then decide retention at collector/gateway based on attributes like `model_id`, `gpu_id`, `seq_len`, and error/latency. This reduces backend load while keeping fidelity for interesting traces.
sre-ops: Tail-based sampling requires buffering. We need to estimate memory footprint: if we buffer X traces for Y seconds in eu-west peak, what's the increase?
ashok: I ran a quick calc: peak 2k traces/s, avg 150 spans/trace, storing 5s buffer => ~1.5M spans in memory. That's non-trivial; we'll need either aggressive pre-sampling or modest buffer (1-2s) plus deterministic keep rules (errors, latency>1s, model==redwood-13b).
maria: We have an existing otel-collector config in staging for tail-based sampling; here's the sampler snippet we tried:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    decision_wait: 2s
    num_traces: 50000
    policies:
      - name: keep-errors
        type: status_code
        status_code: "ERROR"
      - name: keep-slow-gpu
        type: attribute
        attribute:
          key: "latency_ms"
          op: gt
          value: 1000
      - name: keep-model-13b
        type: attribute
        attribute:
          key: "model_id"
          op: eq
          value: "redwood-13b"
```
park: That looks reasonable for staging. In prod we likely need `decision_wait: 1s` at minimum to avoid high tail-latency.
leo: Also add runtime span attributes at SDK level: `gpu_id`, `model_id`, `seq_len`, `batch_size`, `host_region`. Those fields help sampling and dashboarding.
jordan: SDK quick patch for python: set resource attributes + span attributes in the inference wrapper. Example: `span.set_attribute("gpu_id", os.environ.get("GPU_ID"))`.
sre-ops: Dashboard / alert implications: our traces-per-second metric will drop with sampling; don't use raw trace count for SLO alerts. Instead derive error-rate and latency from metrics (Prometheus) and reserve traces for debugging.
maria: Agreed — we should tune Grafana panels: show `traces_kept_per_minute`, `trace_drop_rate`, and `tail_sampler_memory_bytes` per collector. Also setup alert: if `trace_drop_rate` > 20% for >=5m in eu-west, paging to eng-infra.
devops-bot: deploy job: rollout/otel-collector-eu-west started (id: deploy-9832) :rocket:
ashok: Actionable tasks:
- maria: reproduce with curl + `traceparent` to internal runtime and paste raw headers (ETA 2h)
- park: add nginx proxy_set_header and bump large_client_header_buffers in eu-west testing (ETA 4h)
- jordan: small SDK patch to set gpu/model/seq attributes and reduce exporter batch delay to 200ms in streaming codepath (ETA EOD)
- leo: prototype collector tail sampling with decision_wait=1s and memory metric exposure, run load test (ETA tomorrow)
- sre-ops: add Grafana panels & alert rules for trace_drop_rate and tail sampler memory (ETA tomorrow)
maria: thanks — let's reconvene after the staging run. If headers are preserved but spans still drop, we'll suspect runtime flush behavior or resource eviction in GPU pool.
leo: one more note — make sure ingress LB doesn't rewrite `traceparent` casing (some proxies lower-case headers). We rely on exact header names in some filters. Use canonicalized header lookups in Envoy.
park: copying this into the infra runbook under Observability > Tracing > EU-GPU for future ops. :white_check_mark:
